title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
gist: Apple announced its first major MacBook Pro redesign in over five years, adding an OLED 'PROLED XDR' display and the first touchscreen on macOS, while keeping M5 Pro/Max chips rather than M6. Prices start at $2,899 for the 14-inch M5 Pro and reach $4,799 for the 16-inch M5 Max, shipping November 6.

insights.claim: Apple's redesigned MacBook Pro brings a touchscreen to macOS for the first time, a change Apple long debated and Steve Jobs famously opposed.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A long-held Apple design doctrine has been abandoned, narrowing Mac/iPad differentiation.
insights.quote: it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated
insights.locator: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave

insights.claim: The touchscreen MacBook Pro is not a 2-in-1 convertible; Apple's footage showed users reaching up to touch the screen in normal laptop configuration.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple is protecting the iPad by not making the Mac a tablet.
insights.quote: It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though
insights.locator: Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting

insights.claim: The camera notch is replaced by a Dynamic Island, borrowing the iPhone interface element.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Continued convergence of iPhone UI patterns into the Mac.
insights.quote: the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island

insights.claim: The PROLED XDR OLED display reaches 2,000 nits peak brightness with a claimed 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and keeps a 120 Hz variable refresh rate.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple moving its laptop line to OLED is a demand signal for OLED panel suppliers.
insights.quote: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.

insights.claim: Apple referenced burn-in protection but did not share how it addresses OLED burn-in.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Burn-in durability is an open question for a static-UI desktop OS on OLED.
insights.quote: References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.

insights.claim: The redesign keeps the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips from the prior refresh, skipping the M6 series already in other Macs; reports suggest Apple will wait for M7, which could bring significant AI performance gains.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The next big MacBook Pro silicon upgrade is tied to M7 and AI performance.
insights.quote: there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance

insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Higher entry prices push Mac ASPs up and test premium demand.
insights.quote: The M5 Pro-equipped 14-inch model starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch starts at $3,399.

insights.claim: The 14-inch model weighs about 3 pounds, roughly half a pound lighter, memory still tops out at 128GB, and storage now reaches 16TB.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Spec gains are in form factor and display, not compute or memory.
insights.quote: storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it
